findings.claim: Every ordinary payload write while mode 2026 is active resets the recovery timer, so a continuously emitting producer that loses ESU can suppress painting forever.
findings.evidence: Built @wterm/dom plus committed WASM: BSU+A, 900 ms, then ordinary B had no renderer clearDirty call by 1,002 ms from BSU. The linked contract starts the clock at BSU and extends it only on another BSU; wterm.ts cancels and recreates the timer on every synchronized write.
findings.path: WTerm.write payload → synchronizedOutput true → _scheduleSynchronizedOutputFallback → cancel/recreate timer

findings.claim: After timeout, a later BSU cannot begin a fresh atomic block until the stale prior block receives ESU or reset.
findings.evidence: Built packages plus committed WASM: after BSU+A timed out, BSU+B was scheduled for immediate paint because _synchronizedOutputTimedOut remained true while the core still reported mode 2026 active; only ESU cleared the bypass.
findings.path: fallback sets local timedOut → core remains mode 2026 → later BSU leaves core boolean unchanged → WTerm bypasses hold

findings.claim: A throwing public onData callback aborts write before synchronized timeout and render bookkeeping, leaving that write without a recovery deadline.
findings.evidence: Built packages plus committed WASM: BSU+X+CPR request with onData throwing propagated the error and left _synchronizedOutputTimer null because _drainResponses runs before the synchronized branch.
findings.layer: public callback failure through WTerm write scheduling
findings.path: WTerm.write → _drainResponses → onData throw → synchronized scheduling never reached
